seo.metaDescription: Hurt on the job in Claremont? Get a free review from an attorney to explore workers' comp and third-party injury claims.

hero.subtitle: When a job site injury happens near Indian Hill Boulevard or along the Foothill corridor, sorting out who's actually responsible can be confusing. We help injured Claremont workers understand whether a third party, not just your employer, played a role in your injury.

about.title: Claremont Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Claremont sits in a stretch of Los Angeles County where warehouses, retail centers, and small manufacturing shops line corridors like Foothill Boulevard and Baseline Road, and workplace accidents happen in all of them. Most injured workers assume workers' compensation is their only path forward, and in many cases that's true against the employer. But California law allows a separate claim against a negligent third party, like a subcontractor, a property owner, or an equipment manufacturer, when their actions contributed to the injury. We review the details of your injury, figure out whether a third-party claim exists alongside a workers' comp filing, and explain the options in plain language before any deadline passes.
commonInjuries: Falls from ladders, scaffolding, or loading docks
Injuries from malfunctioning tools or heavy machinery
Vehicle-related injuries during work deliveries or errands
Burns or chemical exposure on job sites
Injuries caused by falling materials or unsafe storage
about.ctaText: Tell us what happened, and we'll review your case at no cost to you.

items.title: We Look Beyond the Comp System
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but it doesn't cover claims against a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker. We check for that separate path and explain your options.

items.title: We Know the Clock Matters
items.desc: Reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days protects your comp rights, and a third-party injury claim carries its own 2-year deadline. Getting started early gives you more room to work.

items.title: We Understand Retaliation Concerns
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report an injury. If you're worried about your job while sorting out a claim, we can explain your protections.

items.question: My employer says workers' comp is my only option. Is that true?
items.answer: Usually workers' comp is the exclusive remedy against your employer, regardless of fault. But if a third party, like a contractor, equipment manufacturer, or property owner, contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim outside the comp system. We can look at the facts and tell you whether that applies to your situation.

items.question: I was injured at a job site along Foothill Boulevard in Claremont. Does location matter?
items.answer: The specific corridor doesn't change the legal rules, but it can help identify whether other businesses, property owners, or subcontractors operating nearby were involved. Job sites along busy commercial stretches like Foothill Boulevard often involve multiple companies, which is exactly the kind of situation where a third-party claim can surface. We can sort out who was actually responsible.

items.question: Can I lose my job for reporting a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: No, retaliation against a worker for reporting an injury is illegal under California law. If you believe your employer is punishing you for filing a report or seeking treatment, that's worth raising with us right away. Documenting the timeline of events can help support your position.
